observations.where: DS-type·C3–C5, wordmark, social-wordmark and social-tagline rows
observations.observation: The wordmark uses the platform monospace stack, so it renders as SF Mono or Menlo, while the tagline at C5 falls back to a Courier-like face; neither matches the DM Mono used in every watch frame.
observations.why: The brand's most visible type is the least controlled, and the Courier tagline looks like an unstyled default beside the refined UI mono.
observations.change: Self-host one mono face (see Q1) and use it for the wordmark at 600, 30px, letter-spacing -0.01em. Set the social wordmark at 700, 64px, letter-spacing -0.02em, and the tagline at 400, 30px, line-height 1.45. Remove the ui-monospace-first `wordmark` family.

observations.where: B·A2 finished progress bar, B·E3 '+34 pts vs baseline', D2·A4–A5 'trial is best' lines
observations.observation: Green #4FA97A fills the full-width finished bar and colors the delta lines, while orange diamonds mark the same 'best' values, so two accents claim one meaning.
observations.why: The references work because they keep one strong accent; here green competes with the brand orange at exactly the moment the run lands.
observations.change: Limit success green to the '✓ Finished' word and its check. Draw the 100% progress fill in fg-tertiary #939AB0 at 3px (light: #7C8399). Set delta and 'trial is best' text in muted #A8AEBD with only the numeral in fg, and keep orange #F0764B as the sole highlight.

observations.where: A·C4–E7, cell brackets around sample boxes; DS-components·B2
observations.observation: The cell brackets read as thin 1px text-glyph `[ ]` strokes with square ends, while the logo brackets are stroke-4 polylines with round caps and short horizontal arms.
observations.why: The bracket-matrix idea is the product's signature, but in the matrix it looks like punctuation rather than a drawn mark.
observations.change: Draw cell brackets as SVG polylines: stroke 1.5px, round caps, arm length 4px (about 8/48 of the 20px box-row height, matching the logo's 8/48 ratio), color fg-tertiary #939AB0 at 70%, and 3px gap to the first box.

observations.where: A·C5–E7 and B'·C7–E7, queued cells versus started cells
observations.observation: Started cells sit on a filled raised #1F2440 ground while queued cells get a 1px outline, so the lower half of the matrix becomes a wall of outlined rectangles that is louder than the cells with results.
observations.why: Waiting work outranks finished work visually, and the mix of fill and outline creates a checkerboard texture.
observations.change: Give queued cells no border and a transparent ground so only their boxes and 'queued' label show. Keep raised #1F2440 for cells with any started sample, and drop the cell outline entirely except for focus.

observations.where: A·C4 and E4 group rule under '65% · 4/15'; B'·C3–E8 group summary rules
observations.observation: Complete group rows show a bright, near-fg 2px rule across the full column width, which repeats down B' like a stack of white underlines.
observations.why: It is the brightest line on the page yet carries the least news, and it fights the orange progress bar above.
observations.change: Render the group bar as 2px with track line #2A3053. Fill completed groups in fg-tertiary #939AB0 at 50% opacity, and fill in-progress groups in accent #F0764B.

observations.where: A·A4–A6 and B'·A3–A8, group name column
observations.observation: The 'N evals' count and 'trial-only' chip sometimes sit inline and sometimes wrap below, and 'claude-cloud-orchestrator/' pushes '1 evals' to its own line, so the left edge and row heights are ragged.
observations.why: Diagram-like structure depends on every row having the same anatomy.
observations.change: Always put the group name on line 1 (14px/500) and the count plus chip on line 2 (12px/400, 4px top gap). Set the chip to 11px, padding 1px 5px, radius 3px and a 1px line #2A3053 border, and fix group row height at 52px.

observations.where: C·E3–E7, drawer section labels 'Assertions', 'Phases', 'Recent output'; B·A3 'Leaderboard'
observations.observation: Section labels are 13px DM Sans 500 in muted gray and read like generic app headings.
observations.why: Warp's bracketed figure captions ('[ fig. 1 — the factory ]') and Tailscale's small mono labels are exactly what would make benchspec feel like an engineering diagram, and the brackets are already ours.
observations.change: Set section labels as mono 11px/500, letter-spacing 0.06em, lowercase, fg-tertiary #939AB0, wrapped in brackets: '[ assertions · 3 failed · 6 passed ]', with 12px space below.

observations.where: C·E3 drawer title path and C·E8 footer path
observations.observation: 'plan-review-judges-findings' breaks mid-word at a hyphen, and the sample path at the foot wraps arbitrarily in a pinkish tint.
observations.why: Ragged breaks in the drawer's most prominent line look unfinished.
observations.change: Insert <wbr> after each '/' and use overflow-wrap: anywhere only as a fallback. Show the path at 12px/1.45 in fg-tertiary #939AB0, not tinted, with the eval leaf in fg #E8ECF1 at 500.

observations.where: B·A3–F5, leaderboard table grounds
observations.observation: The table stacks three grounds (lbl #171A31, band #181B34, surface #1B1F3B) with banded rows, giving a striped, heavy block around very few numbers.
observations.why: Stripe-style precision comes from rules and alignment, not alternating fills, and the banding blurs the orange 'best' highlight.
observations.change: Use one surface #1B1F3B ground with 1px line #2A3053 rules between rows and no band or lbl fills. Use 20px vertical cell padding and tabular-nums. Set metric labels at 13px muted, and numbers at 18px/500 right-aligned on a shared decimal edge.

observations.where: DS-colors dark·E8 accent vs B2 brand-orange; DS-colors light·E8–H8 accent and accent-ink
observations.observation: The page uses four oranges: brand #E85D2F, dark accent #F0764B, light accent #D8430F (redder and hotter) and accent-ink #A93F18 (brown). The light theme's orange in A-light·C4 reads closer to red than the brand.
observations.why: The single strong accent loses identity when each theme shifts its hue.
observations.change: Keep hue at about 15°. Dark accent stays #F0764B. Light accent becomes the brand #E85D2F for marks and bars, and light accent-ink becomes #B84A1E for text, so hue holds and only lightness moves.

observations.where: A-light·C4 timeout and quiet boxes; DS-colors light·E2 warn #806100
observations.observation: Light warn #806100 renders olive-brown, and light pass #5E657B fills render as heavy dark slate squares (A-light·E4), which inverts the 'quiet pass' idea.
observations.why: The light theme looks muddy and its loudest marks are the boring ones.
observations.change: Set light warn to amber #9A6700 (warn-tint #FBF0D6). Lighten light status-pass to #7C8399, keeping 3:1 on the new raised color, so passes recede as they do in dark.

observations.where: DS-cover·E3–H4 palette blocks; A·H2 'Light theme' pill
observations.observation: On the cover, the orange block touches the card's top edge and the slab block runs past the right edge, so the cover looks cropped. Elsewhere, the theme toggle is the only fully rounded pill among 4px controls and 8px panels.
observations.why: Edge collisions and one-off radii make a precise system look accidental.
observations.change: Inset all cover blocks 24px from the card edges on an 8px gutter, and keep them at radius 8px. Set the theme toggle to radius 4px to match the Copy buttons. Codify radii as 2px (boxes), 4px (controls, cells, chips) and 8px (panels, cards, drawer).

top_three: Adopt IBM Plex Mono as the single mono face for wordmark (600), data and labels. Drop the platform-stack wordmark and the Courier-looking tagline so the brand type is one controlled voice.

Re-tone the light theme to warm paper (bg #F6F4EF, surface #FDFCF9, raised #EEEBE4, line #DCD7CC). Fix its accent to brand #E85D2F, warn to #9A6700 and pass to #7C8399 so it stands on its own instead of looking muddy and cool.

Enforce one accent and extend the bracket vocabulary. Take green off the finished bar and delta lines, quiet completed group rules and queued-cell outlines, and draw cell brackets as round-capped 1.5px SVG with bracketed mono section captions, so the bracket-matrix idea shows up across the whole page.

observations.observation: Best values get an orange diamond, orange value text, and the word 'best' — three orange marks per winning cell, so the leaderboard's right column is a wall of orange (99%, 37/38, plus deltas).
observations.why: The accent token's own rule is 'a mark, never text'; using accent for value, glyph and label simultaneously dilutes it and fights the orange progress bar and live dot.
observations.change: Keep the ◆ diamond + value in accent #F0764B, but set the word 'best' in muted #8B93A7 and drop the orange from '1.53× best' ratio lines to fg-tertiary #939AB0.

observations.where: A·B2, 40% counter and progress bar
observations.observation: The 44px counter, the '31 of 78 finished' beside it, and the full-width 3px progress bar are strong, but the bar's orange fill ends abruptly mid-track with no tick or marker at the finish position.
observations.why: Warp's diagram quality comes from small precise marks; the bar is the one hero element and it currently reads as a plain CSS progress element.
observations.change: Add a 1px tick in fg #E8ECF1 at the leading edge of the fill (full bar height + 2px), and set the track to line #2A3053 at 2px with the fill at 3px so the fill visibly overhangs the track.

observations.where: C·F6, drawer phase bar
observations.observation: The phase bar stacks bind/boot/setup/agent/grade as adjacent color blocks (gray, orange, gray) with no gaps and no per-segment labels on the bar itself; the orange agent segment dominates and reads as 'progress' rather than 'time spent'.
observations.why: It visually collides with the run progress bar above it — two orange horizontal bars meaning different things on one screen.
observations.change: Separate segments with 1px bg-colored gaps, reduce bar height to 4px, and reserve accent orange only for the agent segment while bind/boot/setup use fg-tertiary #939AB0 at 60/40/25% opacity and grade uses note #A5ACBE.

observations.where: A·G4, hover card
observations.observation: The hover card floats on bg with a 1px line border and no shadow, so over the matrix its edges are hard to parse against the raised cells beneath it.
observations.why: On a dark theme, elevation without shadow reads flat; the card's sample rows visually merge with the matrix rows behind.
observations.change: Give popovers/drawers a shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(11,13,31,0.5) plus the existing 1px line border, and raise the card ground from bg #14172E to raised #1F2440.

observations.where: D2·A4–B5, phone leaderboard bars
observations.observation: The per-arm pass-rate bars (baseline gray, trial orange) are good, but the gray baseline bar uses the same fill as the track behind it, so its 65% length is only legible via the endpoint.
observations.why: On the small screen the bars are the whole story; the losing arm's bar nearly disappears.
observations.change: Set the non-best arm's bar fill to #6E7891 (wm-left) against a track of raised #1F2440, and round only the trailing cap (radius 2px) so length reads crisply.

observations.where: A·A7, legend row
observations.observation: The nine-state legend sits at the bottom edge in 12px muted text with glyphs at the same size as labels, and it crowds the matrix's last row (send-findings-back at A6 nearly touches it).
observations.why: The legend is the key to the whole shape language; treating it as footer noise undersells the system's most distinctive element.
observations.change: Give the legend its own band: 8px vertical padding, 1px line #2A3053 top border, glyphs at 14px with 6px glyph-to-label gap and 18px between items.

observations.where: DS-type·B3 vs A·B1, wordmark vs UI mono
observations.observation: The wordmark uses the platform monospace stack while all UI data uses DM Mono, so the logo in the top bar (A·B1) is set in a visibly different face from the iteration_12 text beside it.
observations.why: Two monos in one 14px line reads as a rendering bug, not a system; the references all use one mono voice.
observations.change: Set the wordmark in the chosen UI mono (see Q1) at weight 500 with -0.01em tracking, and reserve the platform stack only as fallback.

observations.where: A-light·C4, selected cell ring
observations.observation: The selected cell's 2px accent ring (#D8430F in light) plus the orange progress bar and orange live dot put three saturated oranges in the top half of the light page, where orange is louder than on navy.
observations.why: On paper tones the accent needs more restraint; the light theme currently inherits dark-theme accent density.
observations.change: In light theme only, render the selected ring as 2px brand-navy #1B1F3B with a 1px accent inner offset, keeping orange for the live dot and progress fill.

observations.where: B'·C3–E7, full-suite matrix rows
observations.observation: At 232-cell scale the matrix holds up, but every row is the same height whether it carries live state (running, fails) or is a plain queued row, so the eye gets no rhythm of importance down the page.
observations.why: Stripe's docs get their calm from varied vertical rhythm; uniform 34px rows at this density feel like a spreadsheet dump.
observations.change: Compress queued/n-a rows to 28px and keep rows containing running/failed/error samples at 36px, with group summary rows at 40px and 500 weight — density stays, hierarchy appears.

Q1.why: IBM Plex Mono has the most character of the three without getting quirky: the slightly condensed proportions and the distinctive lowercase (the curved-tail l, the open g) give data a designed voice that DM Mono's neutral roundness and JetBrains Mono's wide, IDE-familiar texture both lack. It also pairs best with DM Sans — both have a engineered-but-warm tone that matches the navy/orange brand and the Tailscale-style small mono labels in the references. Numerals in the 40%/99% counters stay crisp at 400/500, and its brackets and slashes (heavy in eval ids like delegating-to-codex/plan-review-judges-findings) are the cleanest of the three. Adopt it for wordmark, data and labels so the top bar stops mixing two monos.

Q2.answer: Warp's diagram framing: the small bracketed figure caption ('[ fig. 1 — the factory ]') and the dot-matrix texture that make the page read like an engineering drawing.
Q2.where: Two places. (1) A bracketed mono caption above the matrix in A·B3, e.g. '[ matrix — 232 cells · 2 arms ]' in 12px muted #8B93A7, which also reinforces the bracket motif at page scale. (2) A faint 16px dot grid (dots at 4% fg opacity) behind the empty right region of the leaderboard (B·G3–H5) and behind PageState empty states, so large empty areas feel intentional rather than unfinished.

Q3.answer: Yes — the current cool blue-gray ramp (#F3F4F8 / #FFFFFF / #E9EBF2) reads as a default light mode; the references' warmth is the single biggest gap between the light theme and the stated taste targets.
Q3.values: bg #F7F5F0, surface #FFFFFF, raised #F0EDE6, band #F3F0E9, hover #EDEAE2, line #E3DFD5, lbl #EAE6DC; keep fg #1B1F3B, muted #5A6070 (warmed from #4A5262), accent #D8430F, accent-ink #A93F18. brand-paper for social cards becomes #F7F5F0 to match.

top_three: Warm the light theme to paper tones (bg #F7F5F0, raised #F0EDE6, line #E3DFD5) so it stands with the references instead of reading as an inverted dark theme.
Adopt IBM Plex Mono as the single mono for wordmark, data and labels, ending the platform-stack/DM-Mono split visible in the top bar.

Pull the bracket-matrix motif up to page level — bracketed mono caption over the matrix and bracket caps on the column-header row — while thinning the leaderboard's triple-orange 'best' treatment to diamond + value only.

observations.where: FONT-1·A2 and G4, progress and hover-card percentages; FONT-2·A2 and G4; DS-type part 1·B2–D4, wordmark family
observations.observation: DM Mono’s slashed zeros make the large percentages unusually busy, while the wordmark uses a separate platform-monospace voice.
observations.why: The identity would feel more authored if its wordmark, counters and small technical labels shared one deliberate face.
observations.change: Set family-mono and family-wordmark to self-hosted IBM Plex Mono; use 400 for data, 500 for group labels and metrics, and 600 for the wordmark, retaining DM Sans for prose and navigation. Keep the 44px live counter and 30px finished counter, with tabular lining numerals and 0 letter-spacing. Regenerate wordmark assets with the chosen face embedded or outlined and update the platform-font usage rule.

observations.where: A-light·A2–F6, page and matrix surfaces; DS-colors light part 1·A6–F7, neutral surface tokens
observations.observation: The white canvas, lavender-gray cells and cool hover card make the light theme feel like an inversion of dark rather than a paper-toned companion.
observations.why: The cool neutral stack distances the theme from the references’ warmth and makes the orange feel more abrupt.
observations.change: Set light bg to #F6F4EF, surface to #FFFDFA, raised to #EFEEE8, hover to #E7E5DD, band to #F4F2EC, lbl to #ECEAE3 and line to #D8D6CE. Use surface for floating cards, retain navy #1B1F3B as primary ink, and leave the fixed brand orange #E85D2F unchanged.

observations.where: A·C4–F7, matrix cells; DS-components dark part 1·A3–H4, MatrixCell specimens
observations.observation: The bracketed sample groups sit inside repeated rounded rectangles, so the generic cell containers compete with the product’s distinctive small-scale geometry.
observations.why: The matrix reads more like a stack of UI cards than the precise benchmark diagram suggested by the logo.
observations.change: Make idle queued-cell backgrounds and outer borders transparent while retaining every outlined sample square; keep completed-cell fills, hover fills and the existing focus treatment. Standardize cell radius at 4px, sample boxes at 14px with 2px radii, sample gaps at 4px, and bracket-to-label spacing at 8px. Draw brackets as consistent 1px strokes, 20px tall with 4px arms, retaining all distinct state shapes.

observations.where: A·C4, failed and running samples; DS-colors dark part 2·A1–D2 and A6–H7, danger and status tokens
observations.observation: The pink failure marks introduce a noticeably cooler, candy-like accent beside the orange running marks and ochre warnings.
observations.why: That temperature jump makes a busy mixed-state row feel more multicolored than the restrained brand palette suggests.
observations.change: Warm dark danger from #F27089 to #EE7D79 and danger-tint from #3A2236 to #39262D; keep status-fail and status-error aliased to danger. Retain the neutral pass color, ochre warning color and orange running color, without adding further hues or changing state shapes.

observations.where: B dark part 1·D3–F5, winning leaderboard values; D2·A4–C7, best-value annotations
observations.observation: Winning results receive an orange diamond, orange value and repeated orange “best” label, with green explanatory lines adding another layer of emphasis.
observations.why: The repeated decoration competes with the numbers instead of letting the comparison carry the hierarchy.
observations.change: Keep winning values in accent-ink at weight 500, but render the “best” annotation in muted at 12px/16px and reduce the diamond to a fixed 6px mark with a 6px gap. On phone, make the explanatory sentence muted and color only the signed delta in success; preserve all result information.

observations.where: A·A2–F3, tally-to-tabs spacing and matrix column header; D2·A3–C3, tally-to-tabs spacing
observations.observation: Large vertical pauses above the tabs and inside the matrix header contrast with the tightly packed evaluation rows below.
observations.why: The upper page feels loosely assembled rather than sharing the matrix’s deliberate data-tool rhythm.
observations.change: Use 24px from the tally line to the tab strip, a 40px tab-strip height, and a 64px matrix column-header height with 12px bottom padding. Preserve the current evaluation-row density and 32px desktop outer gutter; use the same 24px section gap with the existing 16px phone gutter.

observations.where: B dark part 2·C4–F6, completed skill-group progress rules
observations.observation: At full-suite scale, the completed groups create a ladder of bright horizontal rules beneath relatively quiet labels.
observations.why: The accumulated line weight becomes a competing visual structure rather than a supporting measurement cue.
observations.change: Give group-summary tracks and fills a dedicated 1px height; use #2A3053 for dark tracks and #626B83 for completed neutral fills, reserving the existing orange for active progress. Keep the main run progress bar at 4px so the two scales have an intentional hierarchy.

observations.where: C·F3–H7, assertion list, phase section and recent output
observations.observation: The assertion rows are closely packed, but the transitions into Phases, Recent output and the final path have much larger gaps.
observations.why: The drawer alternates between dense and loose spacing without a clear section rhythm.
observations.change: Retain 24px drawer padding, then use a consistent 24px between sections and 8px between each section label and its content. Set collapsed assertion rows to 36px minimum height, expanded evidence padding to 12px, and evidence/output text to 13px/20px; give the final path a 24px top margin.

observations.where: A-light·G4–H5, hover-card edge and shadow; DS-components light part 3·A1–C2, HoverCard specimen
observations.observation: The light hover card casts a broad, dark shadow that gives it substantially more visual weight than the fine-lined matrix.
observations.why: The floating panel feels like a generic elevated card rather than an annotation attached to an engineering diagram.
observations.change: Use a 6px radius, a 1px #D8D6CE border and box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(27,31,59,0.08) in light. Use the same radius with a 1px #2A3053 border and 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.16) in dark; keep static drawers shadow-free.

observations.where: DS-components dark part 2·A4–E4, controls; A·H2 and D2·B2, theme toggle
observations.observation: The fully pill-shaped theme toggle introduces a softer geometry than the rectangular copy buttons, segmented controls and bracketed data.
observations.why: This isolated radius choice makes the controls feel collected from different component families.
observations.change: Set button, select, segmented-control and theme-toggle radii to 4px, keeping their existing dimensions and focus treatments. Standardize their borders at 1px and horizontal padding at 12px; reserve 6px radii for floating panels.

Q1.why: IBM Plex Mono gives benchspec the strongest balance of instrument-like precision and human character. In FONT-2·A2, the dotted zero makes 40% calmer than DM Mono’s slash beside the percent sign; in C4–F5, labels remain lighter and less insistently code-editor-like than JetBrains Mono. Its 600 weight can also give the wordmark a deliberate voice without introducing another face. Keep DM Sans for prose so the page remains friendly rather than uniformly terminal-like.

Q2.answer: Warp’s diagram-like economy: let measured marks and alignment establish character instead of adding more containers or decoration.
Q2.where: Apply it first to A·C4–F7 and the MatrixCell specimens: remove idle queued-cell outer rectangles, standardize the 14px sample geometry and 1px brackets, and retain fills only where they establish state or interaction. Extend the same restraint to the 1px group-summary rules in B dark part 2·C4–F6. Do not add a decorative dot-grid behind live data.

Q3.answer: Yes—move toward restrained warm paper, closer to Tailscale’s plain confidence, without making the interface cream-colored or nostalgic.
Q3.values: Background #F6F4EF; primary surface and floating panels #FFFDFA; raised cells #EFEEE8; hover #E7E5DD; alternating band #F4F2EC; table-label surface #ECEAE3; borders #D8D6CE. Retain primary navy ink #1B1F3B and fixed brand orange #E85D2F.

top_three: Make the bracketed samples the matrix’s primary visual structure: quieter cell containers, consistent 14px squares and precise 1px brackets.
Unify wordmark, data and labels in IBM Plex Mono, with deliberate 400/500/600 weights and DM Sans retained for prose.
Give light mode its own warm-paper surface system: #F6F4EF background, #FFFDFA surfaces and restrained, warm-neutral elevation.

observations.where: A-light·A1 page ground; DS-colors light·B3 brand-paper
observations.observation: The light theme sits on cool blue-gray #F3F4F8, with white cards and blue-gray lines (#DADDE7, #E4E7EF), so the page reads as a generic dashboard rather than paper.
observations.why: Warp, Stripe and Tailscale are warm or plain paper; a cool ground makes the orange accent look electric and leaves the light theme with no character of its own.
observations.change: Retint the light ground to paper: --bg and --brand-paper #F7F4EF, --surface #FCFAF7, --raised #FFFFFF, --hover #F0EBE4, --band #EBE6DE, --line #E4DDD4, --muted #6B655C, --fg-tertiary #8A8478. Keep --fg #1B1F3B and light accent #D8430F.

observations.where: A·B2 “4 failed”; A·C4 fail marks; DS-colors dark·A2 danger
observations.observation: Fail is a cool magenta #F27089, while the brand is warm orange and the light theme’s danger is already a brick #B53A37.
observations.why: The most repeated mark on the matrix pulls the temperature off the navy-and-orange palette and makes dark and light feel like two products.
observations.change: Set dark --danger and --status-fail to the existing term-red #E25E59; keep light danger #B53A37 as the ink of that same hue. Recolor the X glyph and the “4 failed” tally with that token only.

observations.where: A·C4 selected cell, A·B2 progress, A·G2 live dot, B·E3 best value
observations.observation: Orange is the progress bar, the live dot, the running ring, a 2px selection outline, and the leaderboard winner, all at full strength on one screen.
observations.why: The references use one accent once; here accent, selection and status collapse into the same shout and the bracket matrix stops being the point of view.
observations.change: Keep #F0764B for the progress fill, the 6px live dot and the 1.5px running ring only. Selection becomes a 1px #A5ACBE stroke, radius 6px, no orange. Winners get a 5×5px #E85D2F square, not an orange number.

observations.where: A·C4–E6 matrix brackets; Suite matrix·C3 expanded rows
observations.observation: The cell brackets are a near-invisible hairline, while the same mark in the top bar is crisp, so the matrix reads as rounded status chips.
observations.why: The bracket is the only shape that makes this benchspec rather than a template grid, and at cell size it currently disappears.
observations.change: Draw cell brackets at 1px #A5ACBE, 80% opacity, square caps, matching the logo’s stroke proportion; do not fill them. Leave the box interiors as they are.

observations.where: A·E4 100% pass squares; DS-colors dark·B6 status-pass
observations.observation: Passing squares are a flat cool gray #939AB0, a different gray from the logo’s left column #A5ACBE, so a perfect cell looks disabled rather than like the mark.
observations.why: Muting 100% is right, but a second anonymous gray throws away the chance for every cell to be a small bracket-matrix.
observations.change: Set --status-pass to brand-gray #A5ACBE. Add a 1px top inset #C5CAD6 at 40% so the square has the same slight face as the logo squares, still quieter than a fail.

observations.where: B·E3 99% and B·D4 25.5s
observations.observation: Each best value carries an orange diamond, an orange figure, a green “best” and sometimes a green delta.
observations.why: The diamond is a generic award glyph, and three decorations on one number make the leaderboard look decorated rather than measured.
observations.change: Remove the ◆ and the green “best” label. Mark the winner with a 5×5px square, radius 1px, fill #E85D2F, 6px before the figure. Figure stays --fg; only the delta (“+34 pts”) uses --success #4FA97A at 12px/400.

observations.where: A·G4 hover card; A·C4 cell corners
observations.observation: Cells, the selection ring and the hover card use different radii, and the card floats on a heavy shadow with no edge, like a default tooltip.
observations.why: Mixed radii and an unbordered shadow are the main “unfinished UI kit” tells next to an otherwise strict matrix.
observations.change: One radius scale: cells 6px, cards and drawer 8px, ring 6px. Hover card: 16px padding, 1px solid #2A3053, shadow 0 12px 32px #0B0D1F80, ground --surface #1B1F3B. Path at 12px/500; the 100% drops to 28px/500 with the meta on the next line at 12px #8B93A7.

observations.where: D2·A6–A8 samples and median block
observations.observation: On the phone leaderboard a darker inset starts abruptly at Samples and the pass-rate bars above do not share its edges.
observations.why: The nested slab breaks the one-card column, so the phone frame looks cropped out of the desktop card rather than set.
observations.change: One card, ground #1B1F3B, radius 8px, 16px padding. Separate metrics with 1px #2A3053 only; delete the inner slab. Bars stay 6px tall, track #2A3053, trial fill #F0764B, baseline fill #6E7891.

observations.where: A·A4 group name vs eval ids; A·C3 column titles
observations.observation: Group names, eval ids, column titles and meta are the same small mono weight and nearly the same color, so the matrix has no hierarchy except hue.
observations.why: Stripe and Tailscale get structure from size, weight and tracking; here everything whispers at once and the eye falls on the red X’s only.
observations.change: Group name 13px/600 #E8ECF1. Eval id 13px/400 #8B93A7. Column title 11px/500 #A5ACBE, tracking 0.06em, not uppercase. Meta (“claude-code · sonnet”) 11px/400 #6E7891, 2px under the title.

observations.where: A·A2 “40%”; B·E3 “99%”; DS-type·B6 counter
observations.observation: The counter is the one display moment, but the percent sign is the same size and color as the digits, and the face is light and wide.
observations.why: Numbers are the product; a full-size unit sign makes 40% and 99% look like labels instead of readings.
observations.change: Digits 44px/500, tracking -0.03em, --fg. “%” at 0.55em, weight 400, #8B93A7, baseline-aligned. Same split for leaderboard units (s, $) at 0.65em. “31 of 78 finished” aligns to the counter baseline, 14px/400, 12px gap.

observations.where: Suite matrix·C3 group rules; A·C3 arm columns
observations.observation: The thin rule under a group rate is the most diagram-like mark on the page, but the arm columns themselves are only a gap.
observations.why: Warp reads as an engineering diagram because hairlines, not color, hold the grid; adopting that would calm the matrix without a new layout.
observations.change: A 1px #2A3053 rule on the left edge of each arm column, from the header baseline to the last row. Group summary rules use the same --line token and 1px, inset to the column, not a brighter white.

observations.where: C·F6 phase bar
observations.observation: The phase bar is a  thick orange run with “bind 2.9s boot 7.4s setup 1.2s agent 63.8s grade 15.6s” colliding on one line beneath it.
observations.why: The drawer’s most structural graphic becomes a smear of accent and unreadable captions, which undercuts the otherwise spare assertion list.
observations.change: Bar height 4px, 2px gaps, radius 1px. Segments: setup #6E7891, boot #E3BF5F, agent #F0764B, grade #4FA97A. One 11px/400 #8B93A7 label per segment, 4px below, left-aligned to that segment; drop the single crowded line.

Q1.why: IBM Plex Mono is the one face that can be the wordmark, the cell labels and the 40% counter without looking like a default mono (DM Mono) or an IDE skin (JetBrains Mono). It is slightly narrower and squarer, so “benchspec” locks up tighter beside the bracket mark, and its figures stay even at 12–13px in the matrix. It also shares DM Sans’s humanist stress, so the sans explanations and the mono data feel like one instrument. JetBrains is clearer as code but its tall, quirky drawing would make the wordmark look like every other agent tool; DM Mono is even and wide and gives the lockup no point of view.

Q2.answer: Warp’s diagrammatic restraint: structure from hairlines, color used once.
Q2.where: The matrix arm columns and the leaderboard. Add the 1px #2A3053 column rules, quiet the selection ring and the pass squares, and let #F0764B appear only as the progress fill, the live dot, the running ring and the 5px best square.

Q3.answer: Yes. Move the light theme off cool gray onto a warm off-white, still plain, not cream.
Q3.values: --bg #F7F4EF; --brand-paper #F7F4EF; --surface #FCFAF7; --raised #FFFFFF; --hover #F0EBE4; --band #EBE6DE; --line #E4DDD4; --fg #1B1F3B; --muted #6B655C; --fg-tertiary #8A8478. Light accent stays #D8430F; light danger stays #B53A37.

top_three: Warm the light theme to paper (#F7F4EF / #FCFAF7 / #E4DDD4) so it stands with the references instead of as a cool-gray invert.
Put fail on the warm red #E25E59 and spend orange only four times (progress, live dot, running ring, 5px best square); selection becomes a 1px gray stroke.
Make the matrix the logo: 1px #A5ACBE brackets, pass squares in brand-gray #A5ACBE, hairline column rules, and IBM Plex Mono with unit signs smaller than the digits.
